clue.text: Trailing after a nag?

parts.note: a carriage pulled along behind a tired old horse is literally trailing after a nag

explanation.surface: Someone lagging behind a nagging partner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nag' looks like a scolding person; here it is a horse, and the vehicle trails after it.
explanation.definitionFit: A carriage pulled by a horse is described with this compound adjective, so trailing behind a nag fits it.

clue.text: Ham and wine

definitions.meaning: the joint of a pig's leg, a cut of ham
the British name for German white wine from the Rhine

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses hold: a cut of pork leg, and the traditional British word for Rhenish white wine.

clue.text: Thug chucked coat

parts.note: a rough is a violent hooligan
to cast is to throw or chuck

explanation.surface: A thug threw a coat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coat' is a noun here: a coarse plaster rendering for outside walls.
explanation.definitionFit: Roughcast is an outer wall coating of plaster mixed with gravel.

clue.text: King housed in walled garden

indicators.note: the king's name is housed inside the letters of the words walled garden

explanation.surface: A monarch lives within a walled garden.
explanation.definitionFit: Edgar was an English king of the tenth century, one of several monarchs of that name.

clue.text: Register shows each learner is in RE

indicators.note: the abbreviations are placed inside the two letters of religious education

parts.note: RE is religious education, a school subject
L is learner, as on a learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: A list shows each pupil is taking religious education.
explanation.definitionFit: To register something mentally is to become aware of it, a synonym of the verb.

clue.text: Very small city film properly put together

parts.note: Wells in Somerset is England's smallest cathedral city
ET is Spielberg's film about an extra-terrestrial

explanation.surface: A tiny city's film is well assembled.
explanation.walkthrough: WELLS is a cathedral city in Somerset, the smallest in England.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone well-set is sturdily built, with a well-knit, solid frame.

clue.text: Business putting out English jazz

indicators.note: putting out means expelling the letter for English from the word

parts.note: trade means commerce or business

explanation.surface: A firm bans English jazz.
explanation.definitionFit: Trad is short for traditional jazz, the revived New Orleans style popular in Britain.

clue.text: Engineers start to conduct church survey

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers

indicators.note: start to means the first letter of the word conduct is taken

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Army engineers begin a survey of a church.
explanation.definitionFit: A recce is military slang for a reconnaissance, a survey of ground.

clue.text: Lords' feuds destroyed German city

indicators.note: destroyed means the letters of the two words are wrecked and rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: Aristocrats' quarrels wrecked a German city.
explanation.definitionFit: Düsseldorf is the capital of North Rhine-Westphalia, a city in Germany.

clue.text: Tongue of monkey shortened over time

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits over the second
shortened means the monkey's name loses its final letter

parts.note: a langur is an Asian leaf monkey
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: A monkey's tongue is cut short over time.
explanation.definitionFit: Tongue in the sense of a spoken language, such as one's mother tongue.

clue.text: Held cold part of body

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap
a lung is an organ, part of the body

explanation.surface: A chilled body part was kept.
explanation.definitionFit: Clung, past tense of cling, means held on tightly.

clue.text: Asian cell forged partnerships

indicators.note: forged means the letters are hammered into a new shape

explanation.surface: An Asian cell formed partnerships.
explanation.definitionFit: Alliances are unions or partnerships formed for mutual benefit.

clue.text: Fools don't expect honesty from the cleaner!

parts.note: a char or charwoman is a cleaning lady
you don't expect honesty from someone who tells falsehoods, untruths

explanation.surface: A warning that the cleaning lady can't be trusted.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as 'the cleaner lies', which is why honesty can't be expected. CHAR is British for a cleaning woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A charlie is British slang for a fool, someone who looks silly.

clue.text: Birds — gosh! — going over the Home Counties

indicators.note: in the across entry the first piece goes ahead of the region's letters

parts.note: gee is an exclamation of surprise like gosh
the Home Counties around London lie in the south-east, SE

explanation.surface: Birds fly over the counties around London, to someone's surprise.
explanation.walkthrough: The Home Counties are the counties surrounding London, in South East England.
explanation.definitionFit: Geese are large waterbirds, plural of goose.

clue.text: Looking after mother and saying nothing

definitions.meaning: literally keeping one's mum, caring for her
idiomatically, keeping quiet about a secret

explanation.definitionFit: The British idiom means staying silent, while read literally it means minding one's mother.

clue.text: Model test lots only half completed

parts.note: an exam is a test

indicators.note: only half completed means the word for lots keeps just its first half

parts.note: plenty means lots

explanation.surface: A model exam gets only half finished.
explanation.definitionFit: An example is a model or pattern to be copied.

clue.text: Publicist came across as intense

parts.note: a PRO is a public relations officer, a publicist
found means came across

explanation.surface: A PR agent came across as passionate.
explanation.definitionFit: Profound feelings are deep and intense.

clue.text: Hanging around the bar, Edward stayed behind

indicators.note: the short form of Edward hangs around the bar, enclosing it

parts.note: Ted is a pet form of Edward
a rail is a bar

explanation.surface: Edward loitered at the pub bar and didn't leave.
explanation.definitionFit: To trail is to lag or fall behind others.

clue.text: Old jockey reportedly in city with race course

indicators.note: reportedly means the jockey's name is said aloud

parts.note: Lester Piggott, the famous retired British jockey

explanation.surface: A former jockey is said to be in a city that has a racecourse.
explanation.walkthrough: Lester Piggott was a famous British flat-racing jockey; the city's name is pronounced like his first name.
explanation.definitionFit: Leicester is an English Midlands city which has a racecourse.

clue.text: Rod gets hot working inside pit

indicators.note: inside signals the reworked letters go within the rod's synonym

parts.note: a pole is a rod

indicators.note: working means the letters of hot are set into action in a new order

explanation.surface: A fishing rod gets hot down a mine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rod' suggests fishing, but 'working' yields THO and 'inside' sets that within the rod's synonym; the pit is a cave shaft or road hole.
explanation.definitionFit: A pothole is a deep pit or hole, in a road or in caving terms.

clue.text: Grab drug, having gone to doctor, then run

parts.note: E is ecstasy, the drug
MB is Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor
race means run

explanation.surface: Grab drugs at the doctor's and then flee.
explanation.definitionFit: To embrace is to seize or take hold of, as in grab an opportunity.

clue.text: Notice little girl having hesitation, being not so well

parts.note: to see is to notice
Di is a short girl's name, for Diana
er is a hesitation sound

explanation.surface: Spotting a hesitant girl who looks ill.
explanation.definitionFit: Seedy means unwell, so seedier means more poorly, less well.

clue.text: One administering infant baptism maybe in second part of service

parts.note: a prayer is part of a church service

explanation.surface: A priest doing a christening later in the service.
explanation.walkthrough: Infant baptism is often by sprinkling water, which a spraying device also does.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprayer sprinkles liquid, and baptism may be by sprinkling, hence 'maybe'.

clue.text: Chip receptacle being taken around house

indicators.note: being taken around means the receptacle word is turned to face the other way

parts.note: a can is a container

explanation.surface: A container of chips being carried around the house.
explanation.definitionFit: A nacho is a tortilla chip.

clue.text: Short piece arrived with ring attached

parts.note: came means arrived
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: A brief item turned up with a ring.
explanation.definitionFit: A cameo is a short piece of writing or a small role in a film.

clue.text: Lighter chaps?

parts.note: a lighter is a flat-bottomed boat, so its crew are the men of such vessels

explanation.surface: Men who are less heavy.
explanation.definitionFit: Bargemen crew lighters, the flat-bottomed boats for unloading ships.

clue.text: Poets getting drunk in bar

indicators.note: getting drunk means the letters are reeling into another order

explanation.surface: Poets getting tipsy in a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' looks like a pub; it is the legal verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To estop is a legal term meaning to bar or preclude someone from asserting something.

clue.text: Crook, object given to bishop

indicators.note: the object's word is given to, placed after, the bishop letter

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
an end is an aim or object

explanation.surface: A crozier given to a bishop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crook' suggests a criminal or bishop's staff; it is a curve or bend.
explanation.definitionFit: A crook is a bend or curve, as in the crook of an arm.

clue.text: Brief signal coming on time, received by the Virgin

indicators.note: received by means the pieces go inside the name of the Virgin

parts.note: the Virgin Mary
an omen is a sign

explanation.surface: A sign appearing on time to the Virgin Mary.
explanation.definitionFit: Momentary means lasting only a moment, brief.

clue.text: Undefined article included in the levy once

indicators.note: included in means the pronoun goes inside the definite article

parts.note: it can refer to an unspecified thing, an undefined article

explanation.surface: An indefinite item is part of an old tax.
explanation.definitionFit: A tithe was a tenth of produce paid to the church, a historical levy.

clue.text: Dispute using low tactics initially

parts.note: to low is to moo, as cattle do

indicators.note: initially means the first letter of tactics is taken

explanation.surface: An argument using underhand tactics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'low' looks like underhand; it is the verb for a cow's sound.
explanation.definitionFit: To moot is to raise a matter for discussion or dispute.

clue.text: British record agent with a ruddy good motto!

parts.note: B is British
an EP is an extended-play record
a rep is a sales agent
ruddy means red

explanation.surface: A British record agent with a ruddy fine slogan.
explanation.definitionFit: The Scouts' motto is this phrase, a good motto for life.
